subject: Documentation confusion for predict.dsm() and possible bug

messages.author: a831f53217f0e2f7
messages.subject: Documentation confusion for predict.dsm() and possible bug
parts:
Hi All,

I'm working on a DSM where the response is "density". While experimenting with predict(), I discovered that it does not return what it used to (before Issue #33 was fixed), and what I (perhaps naively) expected.

Also, I think there's a bug when off.set is not supplied to predict.dsm() (more on that below).

I'm posting here so that other poor naive souls might avoid the same mistake.

Here's a minimal example using code adapted from Len Thomas' posting of Issue 33 here: https://github.com/DistanceDevelopment/dsm/issues/33 where it was realized that the off.set was not being taken into account in models with "density" as the response.



library(Distance)
library(dsm)

# load the Gulf of Mexico dolphin data (see ?mexdolphins)
data(mexdolphins)

# fit a detection function and look at the summary
hr.model <- ds(distdata, max(distdata$distance),
               key = "hr", adjustment = NULL)
summary(hr.model)


# fit a simple smooth of x and y to estimated density
mod1 <- dsm(density~s(x,y), hr.model, segdata, obsdata, family=gaussian())
summary(mod1)
# predict over a grid
mod1.pred <- predict(mod1, preddata, preddata$area)
# calculate the predicted ***abundance*** over the grid. Naively reading the manual I did not expect this to return abundance,
sum(mod1.pred)
#24777.49

The crux of the matter is that after reading the manual for predict.dsm() I unthinkingly expected it to return density in the same units as the data passed to predict.gam() (ie. without multiplying by the off.set) like it used to. However, after looking at the code for predict.dsm(), reading the discussion about Issue #33 at the link above, and the helpful posts from Eric Rexstad here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/distance-sampling/predict.dsm%7Csort:date/distance-sampling/kKp8QG5k3eo/1pYcUpcrpD0J I realized that this isn't that is no longer the case.

Predict.dsm() now multiplies the predictions returned by predict.gam() by off.set, for models where the response is "density" (or one of it's synonyms) . From reading the manual for predict.dsm() I did not realize this. Probably because the last time I used predict() it was before Issue #33 was fixed. I know, I know.... at this point you're thinking "Well, what did you think it was going to do with the off.set??". I guess I just naively looked at the output from predict() prior to the Issue #33 fix and didn't think too much more about it.


Thus if you just want density in the same units as in the gam you just need to do:

mod1.pred <- predict(mod1, preddate, 1)


 I'd suggest modifying the documentation for off.set in predict.dsm() to mention this explicitly:

off.set

area of each of the cells in the prediction grid. Should be in the same units as the segments/distances given to dsm. This will be multiplied by the predictions from the gam. Ignored if there is already a column in newdata called off.set.


And perhaps change the Value section to read:

predicted values on the response scale (density/abundance depending on the value of off.set).

I'll volunteer to do this and add an example (based on the code above) showing what happens for different values of off.set if there's interest from the dsm gods. Or perhaps I should offer to expand the vignette?

Now for the possible bug:

The manual implicitly indicates (and Eric's post here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/distance-sampling/predict.dsm%7Csort:date/distance-sampling/kKp8QG5k3eo/1pYcUpcrpD0J explicitly states) that leaving the off.set out of the call to predict() will accomplish the same thing as:

mod1.pred <- predict(mod1, preddate, 1)

However, when I do:

mod1.pred <- predict(mod1, preddate)
sum(mod1.pred)
# 0!

it always returns 0 (because off.set is NULL by default and multiplying anything by NULL is 0.

I'd suggest the following code from the end of predict.dsm()

 # actually do the predict call
  result <- predict(object, newdata, type=type, ...)

  ## if we have density do the predictions on response scale right
  # grab standard error
  se.fit <- list(...)$se.fit
  if((c(object$formula[[2]]) %in% c("D", "density", "Dhat", "density.est"))){
    # only need do this for type="response" but need to make sure
    # that the standard errors are okay too
    if(type=="response" & (is.null(se.fit) || !se.fit)){
      result <- result*off.set
    }else if(type=="response" & se.fit){
      result$fit <- result$fit*off.set
      result$se.fit <- result$se.fit*off.set
    }
  }

Be changed to:

 # actually do the predict call
  result <- predict(object, newdata, type=type, ...)


  ## if we have density do the predictions on response scale right
  # grab standard error
  se.fit <- list(...)$se.fit
  if((c(object$formula[[2]]) %in% c("D", "density", "Dhat", "density.est"))){

    # make sure off.set has a value before multiplying
    if (is.null(off.set))
      off.set <- 1

    # only need do this for type="response" but need to make sure
    # that the standard errors are okay too
    if(type=="response" & (is.null(se.fit) || !se.fit)){
      result <- result*off.set
    }else if(type=="response" & se.fit){
      result$fit <- result$fit*off.set
      result$se.fit <- result$se.fit*off.set
    }
  }


I can open an issue on GitHub if that's helpful.

Thanks!
Dave

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Documentation confusion for predict.dsm() and possible bug
parts:
Hi Dave, hi listfolk,

Thanks for the thorough bug report and suggestion!

I've added a bit of extra text to the "Value" section of the
documentation, along the lines of what you suggest. (I didn't add your
suggestion for off.set, as I can't put together a wording that's both
simple and technically correct...) The wording is at
https://github.com/DistanceDevelopment/dsm/blob/bf7a4d7eaf6ffa02274a5c46bb02f0b5e952aa79/R/predict.dsm.R#L13

Thanks also for catching the bug in off.set=NULL. I've made some changes
to the code that fix this. If you can run your code and check you get
what you expect that would be ace.

Changes will be in the next CRAN release of dsm. In the meantime the
development version of dsm can be obtained using
devtools::install_github("DistanceDevelopment/dsm")


cheers,
--dave

Dave
